## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 These matches include citations in Buddhaghosa’s *Visuddhimagga* (Paṭhamo bhāgo) as well as several canonical commentaries: the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Modern scholarship similarly notes that this tale of the frog hearing the Dharma and gaining miraculous rebirth is framed through commentary and circulated widely across Theravāda literature and its East Asian transmission via texts such as the *Shanjianlü* [Hsu 2018].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0506a) (§2.1–4.4 ↔ §2341–2351_0); Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Vin01a) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §581_10–585); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0201a) (§0.4–1.4 ↔ §662–663); Aṅguttaranikāye Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0402a) (§0.4–1.4 ↔ §53–54); Visuddhimaggo (Paṭhamo bhāgo) (Anya E0101n) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §1276_6–1280)
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database matches for PA_vv_51 — Pali-internal text reuse data involving the Visuddhimagga and several Pali aṭṭhakathās.
- [Hsu 2018] Alexander Ong Hsu, Practices of Scriptural Economy: Compiling and Copying a Seventh-Century Chinese Buddhist Anthology (2018) — Alternative English title and discussion of the frog story's commentary, transmission, and connection to the Visuddhimagga and Shanjianlü.
